name: Learning-Space Graphs Are Strictly Contained in Convex-Geometry Ideals
scope: Finite one-inclusion graphs, up to signed-coordinate equivalence and suppression of constants.
statement: Every learning-space graph is a convex-geometry ideal graph, and the inclusion is strict.
proof: A learning space is an upper ideal of itself, so it belongs to $\mathsf{Icg}$. The recorded learning-space conditioning yields $K_{1,3}$, which belongs to the conditioning closure and hence to $\mathsf{Icg}$, but it admits no learning-space root.
